description: 1. Introduction: The work plan was established based on an ESA internal "ARTES ScyLight Call for Ideas" and reflects the findings from industry workshops or the consolidation process with stakeholders, like National Delegations, operators, service providers, satellite manufacturers, industry and experts. In addition, the work plan lists activities inherited from the former ARTES ScyLight Element work plans that will be issued under the new legal framework of the ARTES 4.0 Strategic Programme Line (SPL) "Optical Communication - ScyLight". 2.Strategic Activities: A number of activities are identified as of immediate strategic importance as they supportadvancement of optical communications technologies, e.g. towards the "fibre in the sky" vision, or they address system relevant elements. Some of those activities have been addressed in ITTs under the legacy ScyLight Element, but have not resulted in contracts, due to lack of overall budget within the Participating States' allocations. However, those activities are still considered of high strategic value and are listed again (or slightly modified) in the proposed work plan. Furthermore, the SPL Optical Communication - ScyLight is supposed to evaluate the benefits of optical communications in more general terms, also beyond pure near Earth satcom applications. Lastly, ScyLight is aiming to foster the maturity of the industrial landscape in Europe/Canada to prepare for future upcoming markets. Some of those strategic areas are listed below.- Foster Industrial Landscape- Atmospheric Effects- Optical Communication Terminal Technologies- High Data Rate and RF/Optical Coupling- Quantum Communications- Standardisation3. Implementation: Thefollowing implementation philosophy will be followed: Phasing: phasing of the contractual activities may be considered, depending on the risks associated with the development, the maturity of the technologies, and potential early market perspectives. ITTs for activities designated priority B will automatically be generated by the Executive. The planned ITT issue dates are indicated in Annex II; however, baseline activities for which industry and/or Delegations declare an interest will be implemented as a priority. Such interest can be notified directly to the ARTES ScyLight Programme Office. Invitations to tender for activities designated R will only be initiated either: On the explicit request of at least one delegation, or On the initiative of the Executive following consultation of the JCB.

title: ULTRACOMPACT 778 NM RUBIDIUM SECONDARY OPTICAL FREQUENCY STANDARD - EXPRO PLUS
description: The objective of this activity is to develop an ultracompact, secondary, optical frequency reference based on a two-photon transition in Rb vapour at 778nm.Description:Ultra-stable miniature atomic clocks are being considered for space applications. The Rubidium two-photon transition secondary frequency standard has demonstrated interesting performance metrics with a further potential for ultra-low size, weight and power (SWaP) integration.Currently, such an approach is hindered by the lack of miniaturized laser sources with suitable power levels and spectral properties as well as a compact physics package design taking advantage of the full capabilities of the integrated photonics and microelectromechanical systems (MEMS) gas cell technology platforms.This activity aims at exploiting these enabling technologies and developing a further concept of a compact high-performance atomic physics package for an ultra-compact secondary optical frequency standard. The goal of this activity is to provide a fractional frequency stability < 10 - 12 at 1 second integration time implemented using integrated photonic techniques.The following tasks are foreseen in this activity: Evaluate sources of integrated photonic laser systems delivering the wavelengths and the required spectral properties for the defined system approach. Develop Rb cell techniques and technologies targeting an ultracompact 778 nm rubidium secondary optical frequency standard using chip-scale photonic integration. Demonstrate the fractional stability performance achievable using the chosen chip-scale photonic approach. Evaluate chip-scale optical frequency combs with SiN Kerr comb techniques to provide an initial stabilized direct optical-RF link. Provide a packaging solution to maintain the preliminary performance achieved.NOTE: This activityis currently in the GSTP Work Plan but will only be implemented after confirmation of financial support from Delegations. The finallist of participating states will be known at tender issue.
